title: Discourse on Faith
subtitle: From the Catechetical Discourses, opening sections
source: A retelling in our words of St. Symeon's twenty-second Catechetical Discourse, On Faith, and of his teaching on repentance. No public-domain English translation of the Discourses exists, so these are not his words. By the editors of Purify.

sections.title: Hear Me, Brothers
paragraphs: In his Catechetical Discourses St. Symeon speaks to the monks of St. Mamas as a father to his sons, and urges them not to lose heart: the grace the apostles received is given still, now, to those who seek it with faith.
He speaks, he says, not from books alone but from what God has done in him, so that his hearers may know that God is the same yesterday, today and for ever (Hebrews 13:8).
notes: Symeon insists on personal experience of grace, against contemporaries who said the apostolic charisms had ceased. This insistence shaped Eastern hesychasm for the next thousand years.

sections.title: The Light That Was Seen
paragraphs: In the twenty-second Discourse, On Faith, he tells, as of another, of a young man named George who, praying at night, saw the divine light fill the room, and lost all awareness of where he was, seeing nothing but light.
When the light withdrew, the young man was left weeping with joy and longing for it, and from then on he sought it.
notes: Symeon's vision of the uncreated light is the central event of his theology. The hesychast fathers, especially Gregory Palamas three centuries later, drew heavily on these accounts.

sections.title: On Tears and Repentance
paragraphs: He teaches that the Christian life begins with mourning for one's sins, and speaks of the tears of repentance as a washing of the soul.
